sections.h2: Who at Pitt County Tax Administration handles what?
sections.html:
Tax Administration in Greenville does the listing, appraising and assessing, and it also collects current and delinquent taxes. Appeals mail goes to PO Box 43, Greenville, NC 27835-0043, and 252-902-3400 is the number on the appeals board notice.

Work is divided by division. Real Property takes builder exemption forms, Business Personal Property covers farm equipment and similar items, and a Tax Relief Division receives applications for exclusions and deferrals. The county posts an email address for relief questions.

  • Appeals: the formal appeal form and the clerk to the county appeals board.
  • Relief: the Tax Relief Division, or the assessor by mail.
  • Billing and payment methods: ask Tax Administration.

Ask which jurisdictions tax a given parcel, since a house inside a town may carry more than one bill.

sections.h2: How big is the Pitt County housing market?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts counts 86,063 housing units and 74,533 households across 652.37 square miles of land. Owners occupy 51.4% of homes, so renting is nearly as common as owning, and the middle owner home was worth $208,900.

  • Residents in mid-2025: an estimated 182,936, a 6.5% gain over the 2020 base.
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,285.
  • Median gross rent: $993.
  • Typical monthly cost for an owner with a mortgage: $1,467.
  • Adults 25 and older holding a bachelor's degree: 33.8%.

Ask the tax office how a change of ownership affects any relief or present-use file on a parcel.

sections.h2: When is the next Pitt County revaluation?
sections.html:
The county's schedule of values has been in force since January 1, 2024 and runs until the next revaluation, which the county gives as 2028. Improvements made in between are priced under the same statutory standards.

The schedule is a manual of rates, value ranges and guidelines that commissioners must adopt. It covers construction adjustments, market adjustments and land schedules. The Machinery Act defines market value as what a willing and able buyer and seller would agree on without pressure and with reasonable knowledge of the property's uses.

State law (G.S. 105-286) also calls for a review in the fourth year after a reappraisal, using percentage adjustments by category or area instead of appraising each parcel. Ask the assessor whether one is planned before 2028.

sections.h2: How do I take a Pitt County assessment to the appeals board?
sections.html:
Submit a formal appeal form to the county board. Appeals can be filed from January 1 until the board formally adjourns, usually in April or May.

The board is made up of residents chosen by the commissioners and serves as the first step of review. It listens to the owner and to the assessor's office. The county names three grounds: a value above market, unequal treatment against similar properties, and factual errors in the record.

Bring comparable sales, an appraisal if you have one, and photos of the house. You may speak yourself or send a representative. The county's form page warns that anything filed past adjournment is untimely. Dates shift yearly, so read the current notice.

A ruling you dislike can be taken to the statewide Property Tax Commission with a written notice filed a month after the ruling is mailed, copied to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: Which relief programs does the Pitt County tax page list?
sections.html:
The county's relief page spans seniors, disabled owners, veterans, farmland, builders, nonprofits and vehicle owners. Homestead programs require that you own the home and live in it.

  • Age-or-disability exclusion: subtracts $25,000 or 50% of the home's value, whichever is larger, from the house and up to one acre. The page prints an income cap of $39,900 for 2027, measured on 2026 income.
  • Circuit breaker: limits tax to 4% of income at or under $39,900 and 5% from $39,901 to $59,850 for 2027, deferring the remainder as a lien.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off the value for a veteran with a 100% permanent service-connected disability, or an unmarried surviving spouse.

File Form AV-9 with the assessor from January 1 through June 1. Late requests from June 2 through December 31 can be considered when you document a reason, and they go to the appeals board. The county says nothing filed after December 31 can be taken for that year. The circuit breaker is renewed every year and every owner on the deed has to qualify. Deferred tax, up to three years plus interest, is payable on a sale or a death.

Land in the present-use program carries its own rules. The county lists 10 acres for agriculture, 5 for horticulture and 20 for forestry under a written plan, and rollback of the current and prior three years follows removal.

sections.h2: Are there other Pitt County exemptions that could touch a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, the county page lists several that matter when the property is not an ordinary house. Each one has its own form and timing.

  • Builder inventory: a residential builder's gains from subdividing, grading or building a new single-family home or duplex are excluded for up to three years after first listing, and a commercial builder's for up to five, ending sooner at a building permit or a sale. The form is AV-65.
  • Nonprofit and special-use property: the AV-10 application goes to the Tax Relief Division during January of the year you apply.
  • Antique automobiles: a vehicle that meets the county's conditions is valued at $500, with the application due a month after the tax due date.
  • Antique airplanes: assessed at the lower of true value or $5,000.

Because a sale ends the builder exclusion, confirm with the Real Property Division how the end date is handled on a particular parcel, and whether the new owner must file a fresh application.

sections.h2: What do I owe at a Pitt County closing?
sections.html:
Tax on real property falls due September 1, interest-free through January 5, and interest starts after that (G.S. 105-360). The county's relief page cautions that a same-day postmark now requires a visit to a Postal Service retail counter, so do not rely on a late drop in the mail.

The year's lien follows the land (G.S. 105-355). Your closing attorney requests a payoff and takes it from your proceeds.

  • Get a payoff for each parcel and taxing jurisdiction.
  • Check present-use or circuit breaker deferrals, which can come due.
  • Confirm any late relief application was decided.

Cash buyers can close quickly, so request the payoff early, and keep the paid receipts with your closing file in case a later question comes up.

faqs.q: When will Pitt County revalue next?
faqs.a: The county says the current schedule of values holds until the next revaluation in 2028. Confirm the date with Tax Administration.

faqs.q: How do I challenge an assessment?
faqs.a: File the formal appeal form with the county appeals board any time from January 1 until it adjourns, typically April or May. The clerk's number is 252-902-3400.

faqs.q: What is the senior exclusion income cap?
faqs.a: The county page prints $39,900 for 2027, based on 2026 income, for residents who are 65 or over, or totally and permanently disabled, and live in the home.

faqs.q: Is a filing after June 1 hopeless?
faqs.a: Not always. Requests from June 2 to December 31 may be reviewed by the appeals board when you give a documented reason, but nothing after December 31 counts for that year.

faqs.q: What happens to deferred tax if I sell?
faqs.a: Circuit breaker deferrals for up to three years plus interest become payable on a sale, and present-use land owes rollback taxes if it leaves the program.
